types.name: FluidVolumeComponent
types.doc:
GPU FLIP water in a box: the grid sits on the entity (floor at its height,
centred on it horizontally), the water starts as the Fill box (fractions of
the domain), and box and sphere colliders inside the domain are walls it
flows around. The surface is drawn as a mesh contoured from the particles.

members.name: flipRatio
members.doc: 1 = pure FLIP (lively, noisy), 0 = pure PIC (smooth, viscous).

The push-constant block every boids kernel reads, declared once for both
languages in Engine/Shaders/Shared/GpuBoidsParams.hlsli.

types.name: FGpuBoidsState
types.doc:
Agent state as the GPU holds it: xyz and a per-agent scale in w for the
position, xyz and the neighbour count of the last step in w for velocity.

types.name: FGpuBoids
types.doc:
A boids swarm on the GPU: the sample GPU ECS world. Fields Position and
Velocity are GPU-owned; a counting sort into a uniform grid (clear, count,
scan, scatter) feeds a 27-cell neighbour search, then the agents move and
write their draw instances (foliage instance layout) in the same step.

members.doc:
The same step on the CPU — brute force over the radius, which the
27-cell search reaches exactly when radius <= cell size — with the same
fixed-point sums, for parity checks on small swarms.

types.name: FGpuFlip
types.doc:
FLIP water on the GPU: particles carry it, a MAC grid solves pressure with
red-black Gauss-Seidel sweeps, the walls of the domain and the scene's
colliders (a signed distance field per cell) bound it.

types.name: FFluidSurface
types.doc:
The water's surface from the per-cell particle counts: a smoothed density
field, contoured with surface nets (the dual of marching cubes: one vertex
per cell the iso-surface crosses, at the mean of its edge crossings, and a
quad per crossed edge).

types.name: GpuSwarmComponent
types.doc:
A swarm simulated entirely on the GPU (boids: separation, alignment,
cohesion) and drawn from the same buffers through the GPU-culled instanced
path. The agents live in a cube of side 2 x Half Size around the entity and
wrap at its faces. Changing the count, the cube, the radius or the seed
rebuilds the swarm from its seed.

members.name: simulateInEditor
members.doc: Off, the swarm stands still in the editor and moves only at play.

types.name: EGpuBufferRole
types.doc:
Who writes a buffer, and so when the CPU may touch it.
Gpu    — component state the kernels own (positions, velocities). The CPU
writes it once, before the first step, and afterwards sees it
only through SyncToCpu (blocking: waits for the GPU, exact) or
ReadLatched (non-blocking, up to two frames old). An Upload
after the first step is refused: it would race the kernels.
Cpu    — inputs the game authors (targets, parameters); uploaded any time,
applied by the next step, read-only to the kernels.
Scratch — per-step working memory (grids, sort keys); never read back.

types.name: EGpuDomain
types.doc:
What a kernel runs over: one thread per agent, per grid cell, per scan
block, or a single group.

types.name: FGpuKernelDesc
types.doc:
A system: an HLSL compute kernel and the buffers it binds, in binding order
(binding i = bindings[i], set 0). Push constants are the world's parameter
block, the same for every kernel of a step.

types.name: FGpuWorld
types.doc:
Component arrays in GPU buffers (structure of arrays: one buffer per field)
and the kernels that step them, in registration order with a compute
barrier between each. A step is recorded into the frame being built
(Record) so a draw later in the same frame reads its output, or run on its
own and waited for (RunImmediate), which tests and readbacks use.

members.name: RepeatLast
members.doc:
The last `kernels` kernels run `times` times in a row each step — an
iterative solver's sweep.

members.signature: bool Record(const void* params, uint32_t paramBytes)
members.doc:
Records every kernel into the open frame (barriers between, and a
compute-to-graphics barrier after the last). False without a frame.

members.name: RunImmediate
members.signature: bool RunImmediate(const void* params, uint32_t paramBytes)
members.doc:
The same step in its own frame, waited for: Begin/EndFrame, Present,
WaitIdle. Use it outside the engine's frame loop only.
